What you can get

Finding one

About 1 in 1,250 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

Its gene carrot

The file

common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/corvid.json — a data-driven gene, not a Java class. It is listed in the index.json beside it and registered by Genes' class initialiser at startup.

Keyhorsegenetics.corvid
Phasemagical — it adds signed colour in phase 3, after the pigment has resolved
Priority407 — where it sits in the one (priority, key) paint order

What it paints

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.

Corvid

The face carries a white field from the muzzle boundary back over the nasal bone and orbits and on to the poll - the whole length of the head, not a wedge that runs out at the forehead - bounded along the upper cheek and hard-edged along a smooth curve throughout. Below it the muzzle is black to the nostrils, cut square across the nasal bone. Each leg has a white ring immediately above the hoof, with black up the cannon over it, and the mane and tail are black speckled white throughout.

  1. the white field up the face — PARTS × AXIS × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  2. the black muzzle — PARTS, painted with TOWARD
  3. black up the cannon, soft where it ends — AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  4. the white ring at the coronet — AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  5. black mane and tail — PARTS, painted with TOWARD
  6. white points through the hair — SPOTS × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  7. a few coat-coloured streaks through the black — STROKES, painted with TOWARD

Wild type
